<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
## Overview

GDN layers with the flat qkvz layout (Qwen3.5 family) fall back to the unfused speculative-decode path on ROCm because `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp` (#51674) only builds for CUDA. This adds a Triton port with the same signature and uses it on ROCm: a state-update kernel tiled over the value dimension like `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` (tile size chosen from the grid size) plus a small gated-RMSNorm epilogue. It covers every model built on `QwenGatedDeltaNetAttention` with the flat layout: the Qwen3.5 family, Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (table below). Qwen3-Next (interleaved layout) stays ineligible, as on CUDA.

## Claims

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, MTP k=3, 1x MI350X, one request at a time: decode 2.39 -> 2.08 ms/token (-13%), E2E 544 -> 488 ms (-10%), on vLLM main (nightly `77154ca`) with aiter main. The first version of this PR (one program per value head, no V tiling) gave 2.19 ms/token in the same side-by-side run.
- Per decode step on MI350X: copy/fill/cat kernels 1.56 -> 0.31 ms, kernel launches 1008 -> 768, GPU kernel time 7.74 -> 6.71 ms.
- Faster at higher concurrency too: per-step time (median ITL) -12% at 1, -6% at 8 and -6% at 32 concurrent requests, output throughput +14% / +16% / +10% (`vllm bench serve`, 2K/256).
- Numerics match the unfused path: the existing MTP kernel test, parametrized over CUDA op / Triton port, passes for the Triton port on MI350X and MI300X (22/22 each); states are bit-identical to the first version at every tile size, and outputs are too or differ only in the rounding of the norm's sum; MTP acceptance unchanged (2.85-2.87 accepted tokens per step).
- Accuracy unchanged: GPQA Diamond 0.821 (main) vs 0.826 (this PR), needle-in-a-haystack 100% for both at 4K-64K tokens.
- Long context (64K in / 1K out): decode step (median ITL) -12% / -6% / -3% at 1 / 8 / 32 concurrent requests; prefill unchanged.
- MI300X (gfx942): per call, 49-60% faster than the unfused path at 1 request and 25-44% at 32 (table below).
- GSM8K unchanged within run-to-run variation (base 0.854-0.861 over 4 runs, this PR 0.848-0.862 over 3 runs), above the 0.84 threshold in `tests/evals/gsm8k/configs/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-DEP2.yaml`.
- CUDA unchanged: the CUDA op is still used wherever it is built.

## Validation

Kernel test (MI350X and MI300X, ROCm 7.2.3; the CUDA-op cases skip because the op is not built on ROCm):

```
pytest tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py -k mtp
22 passed, 22 skipped
```

End to end: Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (BF16), 1x MI350X, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' --async-scheduling`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`. Workload: 104 image-to-video prompt-rewriting requests (one image + 9.5K-token system prompt, ~180 output tokens, temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 3), one at a time, first pass on a fresh server.

| vLLM | GDN MTP decode | Decode ms/token | Accepted tokens/step | TTFT median ms | E2E mean ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (nightly 77154ca) + aiter main | unfused fallback | 2.39 | 2.86 | 107 | 544 |
| main (nightly 77154ca) + aiter main | first version of this PR (no V tiling) | 2.19 | 2.85 | 112 | 510 |
| main (nightly 77154ca) + aiter main | **this PR** | **2.08** | 2.87 | 111 | **488** |

The three servers ran side by side on three GPUs of the same host. The I2V, profile, GSM8K, GPQA and NIAH runs predate the tile-size rule; at one request it picks the same 32-row tiles, and it leaves states and outputs unchanged in the checks above.

aiter main is used because aiter <= v0.1.25 sends the multi-token verify batch to an unsplit gfx950 attention kernel (fixed by ROCm/aiter#6336, not yet released); without it attention dominates the step and hides this change.

Per decode step GPU time (torch profiler, 39 steps, same servers):

| | unfused fallback | first version | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| GDN kernels | 0.48 ms | 0.78 ms | 0.62 ms (includes the gated RMSNorm) |
| copies / fills / cat | 1.56 ms | 0.31 ms | 0.31 ms |
| other elementwise | 0.48 ms | 0.53 ms | 0.53 ms |
| kernel launches per step | 1008 | 738 | 768 |
| total GPU kernel time | 7.74 ms | 6.86 ms | 6.71 ms |

`vllm bench serve` (base and PR servers side by side; random dataset, 2048 input / 256 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, 4x concurrency prompts, min 32). Acceptance differs between runs because the outputs differ. With MTP each streamed chunk is one decode step, so median ITL is the per-step time independent of acceptance; TPOT x acceptance is shown too:

| Concurrency | Base TPOT ms / acceptance | PR TPOT ms / acceptance | Median ITL (step) | TPOT x acceptance | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2.90 / 2.32 | 2.49 / 2.38 | 6.75 -> 5.93 ms (-12%) | -12% | 314.0 -> 359.2 |
| 8 | 6.75 / 1.89 | 5.66 / 2.25 | 10.92 -> 10.31 ms (-6%) | -0.2% | 971.7 -> 1126.8 |
| 32 | 12.46 / 2.24 | 11.48 / 2.26 | 18.74 -> 17.55 ms (-6%) | -7% | 2150.1 -> 2354.9 |

Long context, `vllm bench serve` with 64K input / 1K output tokens (random dataset, `--ignore-eos`, 8 / 32 / 64 prompts at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32, both servers with `--max-model-len 69632` and prompts neither had cached):

| Concurrency | Median TTFT | Median ITL (step) | Base TPOT ms / acceptance | PR TPOT ms / acceptance | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1834 -> 1833 ms | 7.26 -> 6.42 ms (-12%) | 2.49 / 2.89 | 2.33 / 2.71 | 233.9 -> 242.3 |
| 8 | 1917 -> 1886 ms | 14.65 -> 13.79 ms (-6%) | 12.37 / 2.89 | 13.38 / 2.49 | 524.2 -> 512.5 |
| 32 | 2746 -> 3073 ms | 31.43 -> 30.64 ms (-3%) | 34.51 / 2.78 | 34.18 / 2.75 | 782.1 -> 801.9 |

The 64K prefill dominates these runs, and acceptance on random prompts varied from 2.49 to 2.89, which moves throughput more than this change does. The decode step itself is 3-12% faster and prefill is unchanged; at 32 concurrent requests, time to first token mostly reflects queueing behind other prefills and varied by about 30% between passes. A pass with another prompt seed gave -12% / -7% / -6% median ITL.

GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `--max-concurrency 16`, so MTP verify batches of up to 16 requests go through the new kernel):

| | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Run 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 0.861 | 0.861 | 0.854 | 0.858 |
| this PR | 0.855 | 0.862 | 0.848 | |

GPQA Diamond and needle-in-a-haystack, main vs this PR side by side (both servers with `--max-model-len 69632`):

| | GPQA Diamond accuracy | per repeat | mean output tokens | NIAH 4K / 8K / 16K / 32K / 64K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.821 | 0.808 / 0.833 | 8105 | 33/33 each |
| this PR | 0.826 | 0.828 / 0.823 | 8087 | 33/33 each |

GPQA Diamond uses the OpenAI simple-evals prompt and answer pattern: 198 questions x 2 repeats with shuffled choices, thinking on, temperature 0.6 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20, up to 24K output tokens, 64 concurrent requests. NIAH follows RULER's `niah_single_1`: a 7-digit number hidden at 11 depths (0-100%) in the noise haystack, 3 samples per depth, thinking off, greedy.

Reproduce (on a ROCm image, from the vLLM repo root):

```
pytest tests/kernels/fla/test_fused_gdn_post_conv.py -k mtp
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B --port 8100 \
  --max-model-len 32768 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA --async-scheduling \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8100 --max-concurrency 16
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B --port 8100 --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 \
  --random-output-len 256 --ignore-eos --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 1
```

## Details

Models that take the fused path on ROCm with this change (eligibility is unchanged from the CUDA op: flat qkvz layout, K = V = 128, value/key head ratio 1/2/3/4/8, BF16 activations, at most 8 tokens per verify):

| Model | vLLM model code | GDN K/V heads (ratio) | GDN layers | Validated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B | `qwen3_5.py` | 16/64 (4) | 45 | kernel test |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B | `qwen3_5.py` | 16/64 (4) | 36 | kernel test |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | `qwen3_5.py` | 16/32 (2) | 30 | end to end (this PR) |
| Qwen3.5-27B / 9B / 2B | `qwen3_5.py` | 16/48 (3) / 16/32 (2) / 16/16 (1) | 48 / 24 / 18 | kernel test |
| Qwen3.8-27B | `qwen3_5.py` (`Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration`) | 16/48 (3) | 48 | kernel test |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (incl. FP8) | `vllm/models/qwen4_exp` (same GDN layer, flat layout) | 16/48 (3) | 36 | kernel test |
| Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B | `qwen3_next.py` (interleaved layout) | 16/32 (2) | - | not eligible (unchanged) |


- **Root cause.** On ROCm the layer logs `Falling back to the Triton GDN spec decode path: torch.ops._C.fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp is not built`. The AITER fused GDN path only covers non-speculative decode, so every GDN layer's verify step runs ~8 small kernels around the recurrent kernel: contiguous copies of `a`/`b`, three copies plus a `cat` to unpack q/k/v, a zero-fill, an output copy, and the gated RMSNorm.
- **Kernels.** Two launches. The update kernel runs one program per (request, value head, tile of the value dimension). It reads q/k/v and `a`/`b` in place from the projections and runs the gated delta-rule update over the request's tokens with the same state reads and writes as `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`: start from the state at the last accepted token, store the state after every token, slot index <= 0 means no state. Each tile writes its rows of the output and their sum of squares per token. The epilogue, one program per (request, value head, token), adds the partial sums and applies the gated RMSNorm, the only step that needs the whole value dimension, then writes the `out_proj` input. Recurrent state layout is `[slot, HV, V, K]`, BF16 or FP32.
- **Tile size.** 32 rows per program while there are fewer (request, value head) pairs than CUs, 64 up to 4x the CUs, else one tile per value head. A sweep of 32/64/128 rows on MI300X and MI350X (both head shapes, both state dtypes, 1-32 requests) put this rule within 8% of the best tile size everywhere; a fixed 32 was up to 36% slower at 16-32 requests on MI300X.
- **Wiring.** Same keyword signature as the CUDA op; the layer picks the Triton port on ROCm. `forward_hip` routes speculative-decode configs to the packed fused-norm path (`forward_cuda`); non-speculative ROCm decode keeps the AITER path. Opt out with the existing `VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=triton`.
- **Per call.** Qwen3.5-35B-A3B shape (16/32 K/V heads), 4 tokens per request, CUDA-graph replay, current ROCm nightly image; "first version" is this PR before the review (one program per value head):

  | GPU | State | Requests | unfused | first version | this PR |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | MI350X | FP32 | 1 | 30.0 us | 18.7 us | 11.5 us |
  | MI350X | FP32 | 8 | 46.7 us | 26.8 us | 21.8 us |
  | MI350X | FP32 | 32 | 91.4 us | 71.9 us | 64.3 us |
  | MI350X | BF16 | 1 | 28.3 us | 12.5 us | 10.2 us |
  | MI350X | BF16 | 32 | 68.1 us | 36.5 us | 39.6 us |
  | MI300X | FP32 | 1 | 30.2 us | 21.7 us | 13.3 us |
  | MI300X | FP32 | 8 | 56.7 us | 38.5 us | 33.3 us |
  | MI300X | FP32 | 32 | 145.7 us | 96.8 us | 88.8 us |
  | MI300X | BF16 | 1 | 28.5 us | 16.3 us | 11.3 us |
  | MI300X | BF16 | 32 | 117.0 us | 66.5 us | 65.2 us |

  With FP32 state, the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 default (`mamba_ssm_dtype: float32`), this PR is faster than the first version at every batch size on both GPUs. With BF16 state at 32 requests on MI350X it is 8-9% slower than the first version (one tile per head plus the epilogue launch), still well ahead of the unfused path. The 16/48 head shape behaves the same way.
- **Coverage.** End to end this was run on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B only. The other models in the table are covered by the kernel test, which runs every eligible head ratio (1/2/3/4/8) at TP 1-16, but were not run end to end.
- **CI.** The parametrized test runs the Triton port on any GPU (NVIDIA too), so existing CUDA CI covers its numerics; AMD CI covers the ROCm path where it runs `tests/kernels/fla`.
- **Related open PRs (not duplicates).**
  - #61675 adds an opt-in (`VLLM_ROCM_QWEN_MTP_GDN`), shape-specialized ROCm kernel that also fuses the conv. It accepts only 16/48 K/V heads (Qwen3.8-27B), TP=1 and verify widths up to 4, and raises for any other shape, including Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (16/32). This PR makes the default ROCm path fused under the same contract and eligibility as the upstream CUDA op (head ratios 1/2/3/4/8, any TP, up to 8 tokens). The two can coexist, with #61675 taking over when it is enabled.
  - #61434 defers state stores inside the unfused Triton spec-decode kernel (FP32 state, `mamba_cache_mode="none"`). On ROCm this PR replaces that path whenever the fused path is eligible; the deferred-store idea could be applied to this kernel in a follow-up.
  - #59366 adds a separate CUDA replay op for RecoverSSM and leaves the op ported here unchanged.
  - #60833 / #61325 (Qwen3.8 mono decode on MI355X) run vLLM's GDN core for verify steps, so this change applies there too.
- **Provenance.** The first version of the kernel was written and validated in Meta's internal vLLM fork; the V tiling was added in this PR after review.
- **AI assistance.** Drafted with Claude Code (port, V tiling and tile-size rule after review, test parametrization, benchmarks); reviewed and run by the submitter.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Triton port of the fused GDN MTP decode kernel (``fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp``).
+
+The CUDA kernel in csrc only builds for CUDA 13, so on ROCm every Qwen3.5 GDN layer's
+speculative-decode step runs the unfused path: ~8 small copy/cat/fill kernels around the
+recurrent kernel plus the gated RMSNorm. This does the post-conv work in two launches.
+The update kernel reads q/k/v and a/b in place from the projections and runs the gated
+delta-rule update over each request's tokens (same state reads and writes as
+``fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update``: start from the state of the last accepted token,
+store the state after every token, slot index <= 0 means no state). Like that kernel it tiles
+the value dimension, so a small batch still fills the GPU; every tile writes its outputs and
+their sum of squares. The epilogue then applies the gated RMSNorm, the only step that needs
+the whole value dimension, and writes the out_proj input.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.utils.platform_utils import num_compute_units
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _gdn_mtp_update_kernel(
+    mixed_qkv,
+    b,
+    a,
+    A_log,
+    dt_bias,
+    state,
+    state_indices,
+    cu_seqlens,
+    num_accepted_tokens,
+    out,
+    sum_sq,
+    stride_qkv_row,
+    stride_b_row,
+    stride_a_row,
+    stride_state_slot,
+    stride_indices_row,
+    num_indices_per_row,
+    scale,
+    H: tl.constexpr,
+    HV: tl.constexpr,
+    K: tl.constexpr,
+    V: tl.constexpr,
+    BV: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    i_v, i_n, i_hv = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1), tl.program_id(2)
+    NV: tl.constexpr = V // BV
+    i_h = i_hv // (HV // H)
+    bos = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n).to(tl.int64)
+    num_tokens = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n + 1).to(tl.int64) - bos
+    if num_tokens <= 0:
+        return
+
+    o_k = tl.arange(0, K)
+    o_v = i_v * BV + tl.arange(0, BV)
+    p_out = out + (bos * HV + i_hv) * V + o_v
+    p_sum_sq = sum_sq + (bos * HV + i_hv) * NV + i_v
+    accepted = tl.load(num_accepted_tokens + i_n).to(tl.int64)
+    p_src = state_indices + i_n * stride_indices_row + accepted - 1
+    has_src = (accepted > 0) & (accepted <= num_indices_per_row)
+    src = tl.load(p_src, mask=has_src, other=0).to(tl.int64)
+    if src <= 0:
+        for t in range(num_tokens):
+            tl.store(p_out + t * HV * V, tl.zeros([BV], dtype=out.dtype.element_ty))
+            tl.store(p_sum_sq + t * HV * NV, 0.0)
+        return
+
+    p_state = i_hv * V * K + o_v[:, None] * K + o_k[None, :]
+    b_h = tl.load(state + src * stride_state_slot + p_state).to(tl.float32)
+    neg_A = -tl.exp(tl.load(A_log + i_hv).to(tl.float32))
+    bias = tl.load(dt_bias + i_hv).to(tl.float32)
+    for t in range(num_tokens):
+        row = bos + t
+        p_qkv = mixed_qkv + row * stride_qkv_row
+        b_q = tl.load(p_qkv + i_h * K + o_k).to(tl.float32)
+        b_k = tl.load(p_qkv + (H + i_h) * K + o_k).to(tl.float32)
+        b_v = tl.load(p_qkv + 2 * H * K + i_hv * V + o_v).to(tl.float32)
+        x = tl.load(a + row * stride_a_row + i_hv).to(tl.float32) + bias
+        decay = tl.exp(neg_A * tl.where(x <= 20.0, tl.log(1 + tl.exp(x)), x))
+        beta = tl.sigmoid(tl.load(b + row * stride_b_row + i_hv).to(tl.float32))
+
+        b_q = b_q * tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(b_q * b_q) + 1e-6) * scale
+        b_k = b_k * tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(b_k * b_k) + 1e-6)
+        b_h *= decay
+        b_v = (b_v - tl.sum(b_h * b_k[None, :], 1)) * beta
+        b_h += b_v[:, None] * b_k[None, :]
+        # Rounded like the unfused path, whose recurrent kernel stores it first.
+        b_o = tl.sum(b_h * b_q[None, :], 1).to(out.dtype.element_ty)
+        tl.store(p_out + t * HV * V, b_o)
+        b_o = b_o.to(tl.float32)
+        tl.store(p_sum_sq + t * HV * NV, tl.sum(b_o * b_o))
+
+        dst = tl.load(state_indices + i_n * stride_indices_row + t).to(tl.int64)
+        if dst > 0:
+            p_dst = state + dst * stride_state_slot + p_state
+            tl.store(p_dst, b_h.to(state.dtype.element_ty))
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _gdn_mtp_gated_rmsnorm_kernel(
+    out,
+    sum_sq,
+    z,
+    norm_weight,
+    cu_seqlens,
+    stride_z_row,
+    eps,
+    HV: tl.constexpr,
+    V: tl.constexpr,
+    NV: tl.constexpr,
+    SIGMOID_GATE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    i_n, i_hv, t = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1), tl.program_id(2)
+    bos = tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n).to(tl.int64)
+    if t >= tl.load(cu_seqlens + i_n + 1).to(tl.int64) - bos:
+        return
+
+    row = bos + t
+    o_v = tl.arange(0, V)
+    p_out = out + (row * HV + i_hv) * V + o_v
+    b_o = tl.load(p_out).to(tl.float32)
+    p_sum_sq = sum_sq + (row * HV + i_hv) * NV + tl.arange(0, NV)
+    rstd = tl.rsqrt(tl.sum(tl.load(p_sum_sq)) / V + eps)
+    b_z = tl.load(z + row * stride_z_row + i_hv * V + o_v).to(tl.float32)
+    if SIGMOID_GATE:
+        gate = tl.sigmoid(b_z)
+    else:
+        gate = b_z * tl.sigmoid(b_z)
+    w = tl.load(norm_weight + o_v).to(tl.float32)
+    tl.store(p_out, (b_o * rstd * w * gate).to(out.dtype.element_ty))
+
+
+def fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp_triton(
+    mixed_qkv: torch.Tensor,
+    a: torch.Tensor,
+    b: torch.Tensor,
+    A_log: torch.Tensor,
+    dt_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+    num_accepted_tokens: torch.Tensor,
+    state: torch.Tensor,
+    output_gate: torch.Tensor,
+    norm_weight: torch.Tensor,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    scale: float,
+    norm_eps: float,
+    output_gate_activation: str,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Same arguments and result as ``ops.fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp``.
+
+    ``out`` and ``output_gate`` are [tokens, HV, V]; ``state`` is [slots, HV, V, K].
+    """
+    HV, V = out.shape[-2:]
+    K = state.shape[-1]
+    H = (mixed_qkv.shape[-1] - HV * V) // (2 * K)
+    num_tokens = mixed_qkv.shape[0]
+    num_requests = cu_seqlens.numel() - 1
+    # Layouts the kernels index with (as the CUDA op checks).
+    assert K == triton.next_power_of_2(K) and V == triton.next_power_of_2(V) >= 64
+    assert H > 0 and HV % H == 0 and mixed_qkv.shape[-1] == 2 * H * K + HV * V
+    assert mixed_qkv.dim() == 2 and mixed_qkv.stride(1) == 1
+    assert a.shape == b.shape == (num_tokens, HV) and a.stride(1) == b.stride(1) == 1
+    assert A_log.is_contiguous() and A_log.numel() == HV
+    assert dt_bias.is_contiguous() and dt_bias.numel() == HV
+    assert state.dim() == 4 and state.shape[1:3] == (HV, V)
+    assert state.stride(1) == V * K and state.stride(2) == K and state.stride(3) == 1
+    assert state_indices.dim() == 2 and state_indices.shape[0] == num_requests
+    assert state_indices.stride(1) == 1 and cu_seqlens.is_contiguous()
+    assert num_accepted_tokens.is_contiguous()
+    assert num_accepted_tokens.numel() == num_requests
+    assert output_gate.shape == out.shape == (num_tokens, HV, V)
+    assert output_gate.stride(2) == 1 and output_gate.stride(1) == V
+    assert out.is_contiguous()
+    assert norm_weight.is_contiguous() and norm_weight.numel() == V
+    assert output_gate_activation in ("silu", "sigmoid")
+    # Tile V only while the GPU needs more programs: 32 rows per program while there are fewer
+    # (request, value head) pairs than CUs, 64 up to 4x the CUs, else one tile per value head
+    # (tuned on MI300X and MI350X).
+    heads, num_cus = num_requests * HV, num_compute_units(out.device.index)
+    BV = 32 if heads < num_cus else 64 if heads <= 4 * num_cus else V
+    sum_sq = torch.empty(
+        (out.shape[0], HV, V // BV), dtype=torch.float32, device=out.device
+    )
+    _gdn_mtp_update_kernel[(V // BV, num_requests, HV)](
+        mixed_qkv,
+        b,
+        a,
+        A_log,
+        dt_bias,
+        state,
+        state_indices,
+        cu_seqlens,
+        num_accepted_tokens,
+        out,
+        sum_sq,
+        mixed_qkv.stride(0),
+        b.stride(0),
+        a.stride(0),
+        state.stride(0),
+        state_indices.stride(0),
+        state_indices.shape[1],
+        scale,
+        H=H,
+        HV=HV,
+        K=K,
+        V=V,
+        BV=BV,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    _gdn_mtp_gated_rmsnorm_kernel[(num_requests, HV, state_indices.shape[1])](
+        out,
+        sum_sq,
+        output_gate,
+        norm_weight,
+        cu_seqlens,
+        output_gate.stride(0),
+        norm_eps,
+        HV=HV,
+        V=V,
+        NV=V // BV,
+        SIGMOID_GATE=output_gate_activation == "sigmoid",
+        num_warps=2,
+    )
+    return out

Thanks, good call. Switched to that layout in 66eb7ec: the state update is tiled over V like `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`, and the gated RMSNorm runs as a small epilogue over the per-tile sums of squares. One addition: a fixed 32-row tile was up to 36% slower at 16-32 requests on MI300X, so the tile size now follows the grid (32 rows while there are fewer (request, value head) pairs than CUs, 64 up to 4x the CUs, else one tile per head); a 32/64/128 sweep on MI300X and MI350X puts that within 8% of the best tile everywhere. States are bit-identical to the previous version.

Per call (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B shape, FP32 state, 4 tokens per request), previous -> now: MI350X 18.7 -> 11.5 us at 1 request and 71.9 -> 64.3 us at 32; MI300X 21.7 -> 13.3 us and 96.8 -> 88.8 us. End to end on MI350X at batch 1, decode went from 2.19 to 2.08 ms/token (unfused fallback: 2.39). The description has the refreshed numbers.

@simondanielsson Thanks for the suggestions; here are the results (methodology and full tables in the updated description).

- **gfx942 (MI300X):** the kernel test passes (22/22). Per call (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B shape, 4 tokens per request), this PR is 49-60% faster than the unfused path at 1 request and 25-44% at 32. The tile-size sweep there showed a fixed 32-row V tile was up to 36% slower at 16-32 requests, so the tile size now follows the grid size; with that, FP32 state (the Qwen3.5 default) is faster than the PR's first version at every batch size on MI300X and MI350X.
- **GPQA Diamond** (simple-evals prompt, 198 questions x 2, thinking on): main 0.821, this PR 0.826.
- **NIAH** (RULER `niah_single_1`, 4K-64K tokens, 11 depths): 100% for both.
- **`vllm bench serve` 64K/1K:** the decode step (median ITL) is 12% / 6% / 3% faster at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32, and prefill is unchanged (median TTFT 1834 vs 1833 ms at concurrency 1). Output throughput moved -2% to +4%, mostly with acceptance, which varied from 2.49 to 2.89 on the random prompts.
